review_scope: Full bilingual translator self-review: 237/237 source body paragraphs per language (474 translated paragraphs total), all five titles/decks/entry_doors/chapters, semantic qualifications, examples, quotation boundaries, emphasis, and source link; programmatic paragraph/markup/field checks.

findings: Compared all 237 Chinese source paragraphs as read from the five source snapshots with all 237 translated paragraphs in each language; retained order, separate short and quote-only paragraphs, examples, qualifications, and rhetorical repetition. This is the translator’s self-review, not independent review.

Checked titles, decks, entry_door, and chapter in both languages. Retained the entry-door href ../../../start.html and the sole strong emphasis at episode 02 paragraph 16. No new links, headings, examples, diagnoses, or legal detail were introduced.

Episode 01: retained the distinction between bringing judgment before a person and replacing their judgment; real refusal versus punishment; personal limits versus coercion; temporary delegation versus permanent transfer; narrow emergency intervention, later explanation/questioning/correction, and prompt return of decision-making.

Episode 02: retained the change in burden of justification, risk knowledge versus authority over a good life, different choices despite understanding the same reasons, refusal of consequences not one’s own, and need-specific temporary substitute decision-making.

Episode 03: retained problem-solving versus forming one’s own reasons, appropriate delegation of technical tasks, the helper’s anxiety, proportionate forms of help, and other affected people’s right to refuse cleanup. Paragraph 23 deliberately retains the current source 更能: English better able to bear uncertainty; German Ungewissheit besser aushalten. This conflicts with the following anxiety discussion and awaits the author’s decision; no silent repair.

Episode 04: retained unused help as genuinely refusable, sincere disappointment without an obligation to accept, finite resources and a helper’s right to stop, defined emergency necessity and scope, and no guaranteed place in the recipient’s future.

Episode 05: retained the rejection of suffering as an end or lesson, timely prevention of devastating harm, participation in remedy and shared consequences, dependence benefiting both parties without necessarily being deliberate, and refusal of unlimited buffering.

After drafting, improved German wording in episode 01 paragraph 07, episode 02 paragraph 31, and episode 05 paragraphs 17 and 32. In particular, removed the added implication of moral restitution from 补救 and used Behebung der Folgen; clarified explaining on someone’s behalf; used Fürsorgearbeit rather than an added duty formulation.

Programmatic checks passed for 72/45/42/40/38 p elements in each language, expected inline-tag sequence, source entry-door link, required fields, and no residual CJK in translated fields. No Self-as-an-End instance occurs in these source fields; no translation of that name was introduced.
